The structure is described in space group number 12, C2/m, with Hall symbol “-C 2y”, using fractional atomic coordinates. The supplied input cell is not the conventional monoclinic C-centered cell: it has lattice parameters a = 7.57910791 Å, b = 7.57910791 Å, c = 7.63070205 Å, α = 84.00180497°, β = 84.00180497°, and γ = 116.60908674°. This original cell contains 14 atoms, with declared input composition Cs6Tm2O6. To recover the standard setting used for the atomic description, the frames are related by q_standard = P q_input + s, where s is the zero vector and P has rows (1/2, 1/2, 0), (1/2, −1/2, 0), and (0, 0, −1) up to the stated floating-point representation; thus the standard a-axis is the half-sum of the input a and b axes, the standard b-axis is half their difference, and the standard c-axis is opposite the input c-axis. No additional positional corrections beyond six-decimal rounding are specified.

In the standard C2/m description, there are six independent crystallographic orbits. Cesium occupies three separate fourfold sites. One Cs orbit is Wyckoff 4i, lying on the mirror plane with coordinate form (x, 0, z); its representative position is (0.359243, 0, 0.6508), so its independent parameters are x = 0.359243 and z = 0.6508. A second Cs orbit is 4h, of the form (0, y, 1/2), represented by (0, 0.210469, 1/2), with y = 0.210469 as the only free coordinate. The third Cs orbit is 4g, of the form (0, y, 0), represented by (0, 0.262245, 0), with y = 0.262245. These three inequivalent Cs sublattices therefore place cesium atoms in distinct layers or mirror-related sets: one on the y = 0 plane with variable x and z, one on the z = 1/2 plane with x fixed at 0, and one on the z = 0 plane with x fixed at 0.

Thulium occupies a single fourfold 4i orbit, also on the mirror plane, with coordinate relation (x, 0, z). Its representative fractional position is (0.170221, 0, 0.148984), giving independent coordinates x = 0.170221 and z = 0.148984. Oxygen is distributed over two independent orbits. The first is a fourfold 4i site, again of the form (x, 0, z), represented by (0.100150, 0, 0.859083), so x = 0.100150 and z = 0.859083. The second oxygen orbit is the eightfold general-position site 8j, represented by (0.202283, 0.366549, 0.736230); all three coordinates are independent for this orbit. Altogether, the independent standard-cell description consists of Cs at 4i (0.359243, 0, 0.6508), 4h (0, 0.210469, 1/2), and 4g (0, 0.262245, 0); Tm at 4i (0.170221, 0, 0.148984); and O at 4i (0.100150, 0, 0.859083) and 8j (0.202283, 0.366549, 0.736230), with the C2/m symmetry operations generating the full atomic arrangement.
